investigacion.base:
As of October 19, 2026, nothing is scheduled that would put Trump and Zelensky in direct contact on October 29 or 30. US–Ukraine relations are in an open crisis, and the most recent contact went through Trump's envoys, not the two leaders. On current information the question would resolve **No**.

**Resolution source**
I didn't pull up the Metaculus FAQ page itself, so I can't report what it says right now or date it. Going by the question text, "credible sources" means official White House or Ukrainian presidential readouts or major wire reports, which is the usual Metaculus standard.

**Recent news, newest first**
- **Oct 18:** Zelensky had a call of about 40 minutes with Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. It was the first call between Zelensky and senior U.S. officials since tensions spiked after Trump cut a diesel deal with Russia 10 days earlier. On the call, Zelensky and the envoys discussed possibly holding an in-person meeting in the coming days. Reporting doesn't say whether Trump himself would attend, and a meeting with only the envoys wouldn't count.
- **Same period:** Trump accused Zelensky of targeting Russian diesel refineries and not wanting to end the war. Zelensky has said the Trump administration was behind restrictions on the Starlink and Starshield satellite systems used by Ukraine's military.
- **Oct 10:** Trump called on Ukraine to replace Zelensky, attacking him over strikes on Russian oil refineries that have helped push up global diesel prices. High fuel prices, which followed the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran, have become a political problem for Republicans ahead of next month's midterms.
- **Sept 20:** Zelensky said he and Trump planned to meet in New York, announcing it after a phone call between the two, with the meeting expected during the UN General Assembly. I didn't confirm whether that meeting actually took place. The Sept 20 call is the latest leader-to-leader contact I found.

**Base rates**
- Since 2025 the two men have met or spoken roughly once every few weeks, often less. Known contacts include the March 2025 call, the August 16 and 18, 2025 call and White House meeting, September 2025 at the UN, October 17, 2025 at the White House, late December 2025 at Mar-a-Lago, January 23, 2026 in Davos, and the September 20, 2026 call.
- The odds that any particular 2-day window contains a contact are probably around 5–10%. That rises when a summit is happening or a peace deal is close, and has been lower during past rifts, such as the roughly 2-week gap after the February 2025 Oval Office blowup.

**Scheduled events before October 30**
- I found no Trump–Zelensky call or meeting scheduled. No shared summit is confirmed for October 29–30. The US midterms on November 3 will keep Trump focused on domestic campaigning.
- Possible routes to a Yes: an envoy-level in-person meeting "in the coming days" that turns into a Trump meeting or a call he joins, a breakthrough in restarting Russia talks, or a conference call that brings in the leaders.

**What could change this:** reconciliation talks after the Witkoff/Kushner call, a call to defuse the crisis, or a peace-process announcement. A call during a crisis can happen suddenly, but it would have to land on exactly those two days. I didn't find any prediction-market price for this question.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/18/zelensky-witkoff-kushner-ukraine-russia-crisis)
- [2](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/10/trump-says-ukraine-needs-a-new-president-who-will-agree-to-end-the-war)
- [3](https://kyivindependent.com/zelensky-trump-to-meet-in-new-york-in-talks-that-could-change-a-lot/)

criterios: This question resolves YES if US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky engage in direct leader-to-leader communication — either an in-person meeting or a telephone/video call between the two men themselves — at any point on October 29 or October 30, 2026 (UTC), as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as an official White House or Ukrainian presidential readout or major wire reporting. Any direct bilateral contact counts, whether a scheduled call, a pull-aside, or a meeting on the sidelines of a larger event, provided the two principals personally communicate with each other. Communication conducted only through aides, envoys, or intermediaries (e.g., talks involving Steve Witkoff or other officials without Trump and Zelensky themselves speaking) does not count. If no such direct contact between the two men is reported to have occurred on either of those two days, the question resolves NO.
letra_pequena: Contact counts regardless of its duration, format, or whether a formal readout is issued, as long as credible reporting confirms Trump and Zelensky personally communicated (in person or by phone/video) on October 29 or 30, 2026. A public exchange of statements, social-media posts, or letters, without the two men actually speaking to each other, does not count. Contact occurring only before October 29 or only after October 30, 2026 does not count.
razonamientos:
(a) About 11 days remain. The window is October 29–30, 2026 (UTC), and resolution should be clear within a day or two after that.

(b) The status quo points to No. Nothing is scheduled. Relations are in open crisis: Trump has called for Zelensky's replacement and attacked the refinery strikes. The most recent contact on October 18 went through Witkoff and Kushner, not Trump himself.

(c) The reference class is any given 2-day window during the Trump–Zelensky relationship in 2025–2026. The background describes contact roughly every 1–2 weeks. On that cadence a 2-day window would catch a contact about 15–25% of the time. The research assistant's longer list of contacts suggests closer to 5–10%. During rifts, such as after the February 2025 Oval Office blowup, the frequency falls. I put the base rate at about 8–12%, adjusted down for the current crisis but partly offset by the active diplomacy.

(d) No scenario: the envoy-level talks continue without Trump, who is focused on campaigning for the November 3 midterms. Any Russia–Ukraine talks Washington brokers by the end of October run at envoy level. Trump and Zelensky trade criticism through the media, and any call that does happen falls before October 29 or after the midterms.

(e) Yes scenario: the Witkoff/Kushner track produces a reconciliation, or a fresh round of Russia–Ukraine talks is announced for late October. Trump then calls Zelensky, or joins a meeting by phone, on October 29 or 30, perhaps to show a peace-process win just before the midterms. The Ukrainian presidency, which reliably publicizes such calls, issues a readout.

(f) Technicalities:
- The contact must be the two men personally speaking. A Zelensky call with the envoys does not count, even if Trump is reported as "briefed."
- The timing is UTC dates. A US-evening call on October 30 could fall on October 31 UTC and miss the window. A late October 28 Eastern call could fall on October 29 UTC and count.
- Zelensky's office almost always announces Trump calls, so a contact that happens is very likely to be reported.

Probability: 9%

(a) **Time left:** About 12 days until the October 29–30 UTC window closes, though confirmation could be reported later.

(b) **Status quo:** No direct contact is scheduled for those dates, so if nothing changes, the outcome is **No**.

(c) **Reference class:** Contact roughly every one to two weeks implies a two-day base rate around 10–25%. The recent rift and lack of a shared event make this window less likely than usual.

(d) **No scenario:** Envoys continue the talks, or the leaders speak on a different date, but Trump and Zelensky do not speak on October 29 or 30.

(e) **Yes scenario:** An end-of-month diplomatic push prompts a short, unscheduled call between them on either day.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The dates are measured in UTC. A call counts even without a formal readout if credible reporting confirms it; communication only through envoys does not.

Probability: 10%

(a) **Time left until outcome:** The outcome will be known after October 30, 2026, 23:59:59 UTC — approximately 11 days from today (October 19, 2026).

(b) **Status quo outcome:** No direct contact is currently scheduled between Trump and Zelensky for October 29 or 30, 2026; therefore, the status quo resolves **NO**.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:** Bilateral direct leader-level communications (calls or in-person meetings) between heads of state with regular ongoing diplomatic engagement. Over 2025–2026, Trump and Zelensky have had direct contact roughly once every 2 to 3 weeks (approximately 15–25 times per year). For any arbitrarily selected 48-hour window, the unconditional base rate is approximately 5% to 10%. 

(d) **Scenario resulting in a NO outcome:** Tensions remain elevated after Trump's public criticism of Ukraine's refinery strikes and calls for leadership change in Kyiv. Diplomacy in late October is conducted exclusively via envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Furthermore, with the US midterm elections taking place on November 3, Trump is fully absorbed in domestic campaign rallies on October 29–30 and does not hold a personal call or meeting with Zelensky during that exact 48-hour window.

(e) **Scenario resulting in a YES outcome:** The envoy-level discussions yield a preliminary breakthrough on resuming Russia–Ukraine peace talks ahead of the end-of-October target date set by Washington. Seeking a high-profile diplomatic win or pre-midterm de-escalation announcement, Trump conducts a direct bilateral phone call with Zelensky on Thursday, October 29 or Friday, October 30, which is confirmed by official readouts.

(f) **Technicalities:** The resolution requires *direct* communication between the two principals themselves (phone, video, or in person). High-level meetings involving intermediaries (such as Witkoff or Kushner) without Trump and Zelensky speaking do not count. The call/meeting must take place strictly within the UTC dates of October 29 or October 30, 2026; direct contact on October 28 or October 31 resolves NO.

Given the acute friction in relations, the delegation of talks to envoys, the intense midterm campaign schedule occupying Trump in late October, and the very tight two-day window, the probability of direct principal-to-principal contact on these specific dates is modest.

Probability: 9%
